comment: ageScope: 'neonatal' = label gives neonatal or preterm dosing; 'pediatric-incl-neonates' = label pediatric dosing that the label states includes neonates or starts at birth, not neonatal-specific. Terms like preterm or term are kept as labels where the source gives no numeric cut-off.

bands.label: Loading dose
bands.infuse: IV over 30 minutes by syringe pump
bands.quote: Loading Dose | 1 mL/kg | 20 mg/kg | Intravenous* (over 30 minutes) | One Time

bands.label: Maintenance dose, beginning 24 hours after the loading dose
bands.infuse: IV over 10 minutes by syringe pump, or orally
bands.quote: Maintenance Dose | 0.25 mL/kg | 5 mg/kg | Intravenous* (over 10 minutes) or Orally | Every 24 hours

notes.text: Doses are expressed as caffeine citrate; caffeine base is one-half the citrate dose.
notes.quote: NOTE THAT THE DOSE OF CAFFEINE BASE IS ONE-HALF THE DOSE WHEN EXPRESSED AS CAFFEINE CITRATE (e.g., 20 mg of caffeine citrate is equivalent to 10 mg of caffeine base)

notes.text: Serious toxicity associated with serum caffeine above 50 mg/L; monitor levels periodically.
notes.quote: Serious toxicity has been associated with serum levels greater than 50 mg/L.

notes.text: Monitor for necrotizing enterocolitis.
notes.quote: As with all preterm infants, patients being treated with caffeine citrate should be carefully monitored for the development of necrotizing enterocolitis.

notes.text: Measure baseline caffeine level if previously on theophylline or maternal caffeine intake before delivery.
notes.quote: Prior to initiation of caffeine citrate, baseline serum levels of caffeine should be measured in infants previously treated with theophylline, since preterm infants metabolize theophylline to caffeine.

bands.label: First loading dose
bands.infuse: IV infusion over 15 minutes into a large peripheral vein
bands.quote: Loading Dose: 20 mg/kg is administered by intravenous infusion over 15 minutes

bands.label: Second loading dose if clinically indicated, term infants
bands.freq: once, at least 15 minutes after completion of the first loading dose
bands.quote: a second loading dose may be administered over the subsequent 15 minutes as 20 mg/kg for term infants

bands.label: Second loading dose if clinically indicated, preterm infants
bands.freq: once, at least 15 minutes after completion of the first loading dose
bands.quote: a second loading dose may be administered over the subsequent 15 minutes as 20 mg/kg for term infants or 10 mg/kg or 20 mg/kg for preterm infants

bands.label: Maximum total loading dose
bands.quote: The maximum total loading dose is 40 mg/kg.

bands.label: Maintenance option 1, starting 8 to 12 hours after first loading dose
bands.quote: Maintenance Dosage: starting 8 to 12 hours after first loading dose: 4.5 mg/kg/day given in 2 or 3 divided doses (i.e., 1.5 mg/kg every 8 hours or 2.25 mg/kg every 12 hours) up to 5 days.

bands.label: Maintenance option 2, starting 8 to 12 hours after first loading dose
bands.quote: Maintenance Dosage: starting 8 to 12 hours after first loading dose: 4.5 mg/kg/day given in 2 or 3 divided doses (i.e., 1.5 mg/kg every 8 hours or 2.25 mg/kg every 12 hours) up to 5 days.

notes.text: SEZABY contains no benzyl alcohol or propylene glycol.
notes.quote: SEZABY does not contain benzyl alcohol or propylene glycol.

bands.label: Status epilepticus loading dose, pediatric (birth to less than 17 years)
bands.infuse: 2 mg PE/kg/min or 150 mg PE/min, whichever is slower
bands.quote: Pediatric (Birth to less than 17 years of age) 15 mg PE/kg to 20 mg PE/kg 2 mg PE/kg/min, or 150 mg PE/min, whichever is slower

bands.label: Non-emergent loading dose, pediatric (birth to less than 17 years)
bands.infuse: 1 to 2 mg PE/kg/min or 150 mg PE/min, whichever is slower
bands.quote: Pediatric (Birth to less than 17 years of age) 10 mg PE/kg to 15 mg PE/kg 1 mg PE/kg/min to 2 mg PE/kg/min, or 150 mg PE/min, whichever is slower

bands.label: Initial maintenance dose, 12 hours after the loading dose
bands.freq: once, 12 hours after the loading dose
bands.quote: Initial Maintenance Dosage: 2 mg PE/kg to 4 mg PE/kg (dose given 12 hours after the loading dose)

bands.label: Maintenance after initial maintenance dose
bands.quote: Maintenance Dosage after Initial Maintenance Dosage: 4 mg PE/kg/day to 8 mg PE/kg/day in divided doses (continued every 12 hours after initial maintenance dose)

notes.text: Maximum IV rate in pediatric patients: 2 mg PE/kg/min or 150 mg PE/min, whichever is slower (cardiovascular risk).
notes.quote: The rate of intravenous CEREBYX administration should not exceed 150 mg phenytoin sodium equivalents (PE) per minute in adults and 2 mg PE/kg/min (or 150 mg PE/min, whichever is slower) in pediatric patients

notes.text: Intramuscular fosphenytoin should ordinarily not be used in pediatric patients.
notes.quote: Intramuscular administration of CEREBYX should ordinarily not be used in pediatric patients.

regimens.indication: Sedation of intubated neonates in critical care

bands.label: Starting infusion rate, neonates less than 32 weeks
bands.quote: continuous intravenous infusions of midazolam injection should be initiated at a rate of 0.03 mg/kg/hr (0.5 mcg/kg/min) in neonates <32 weeks

bands.label: Starting infusion rate, neonates more than 32 weeks
bands.quote: 0.06 mg/kg/hr (1 mcg/kg/min) in neonates >32 weeks

notes.text: No IV loading doses in neonates; the infusion may be run more rapidly for the first several hours instead.
notes.quote: Intravenous loading doses should not be used in neonates, rather the infusion may be run more rapidly for the first several hours to establish therapeutic plasma levels.

notes.text: Do not give by rapid injection in neonates: severe hypotension and seizures reported, especially with fentanyl.
notes.quote: Midazolam should not be administered by rapid injection in the neonatal population. Severe hypotension and seizures have been reported following rapid intravenous administration

notes.text: Contains benzyl alcohol; gasping syndrome linked to benzyl alcohol dosages above 99 mg/kg/day in neonates.
notes.quote: has been associated with benzyl alcohol dosages greater than 99 mg/kg/day in neonates and low-birth-weight neonates.

notes.text: Extreme caution sedating non-intubated preterm and former preterm infants (apnea).
notes.quote: Due to an increased risk of apnea, extreme caution is advised when sedating preterm and former preterm patients whose trachea is not intubated.

bands.label: Starting infusion, patients less than 1 year old including neonates
bands.quote: Patients less than 1 year old, including neonates: • Initiate treatment in a dosing range of 0.005 mg/kg/hour to 0.01 mg/kg/hour.

notes.text: Monitor cardiorespiratory function in patients under 3 months; titrate to pain relief and somnolence.
notes.quote: Cardiorespiratory function should be monitored in patients less than 3 months of age.

notes.text: Premature and former premature infants with chronic lung disease up to 5 to 6 months: monitor for depressed hypoxic drive.
notes.quote: For premature infants and former premature infants with chronic lung disease and up to 5 to 6 months of age, careful monitoring for depressed hypoxic drive is required following opioid administration

bands.label: Neonates born at 32 weeks GA or more, up to 28 days chronological age
bands.quote: Neonates, including premature neonates born at greater than or equal to 32 weeks gestational age, up to 28 days chronological age: the recommended dosage of Acetaminophen Injection is 12.5 mg /kg every 6 hours, to a maximum daily dose of acetaminophen of 50 mg/kg per day, with a minimum dosing interval of 6 hours.

notes.text: Maximum daily dose counts acetaminophen from all routes and all products.
notes.quote: Calculated maximum daily dose of acetaminophen is based on all routes of administration (i.e. intravenous, oral, and rectal) and all products containing acetaminophen.

regimens.indication: Closure of clinically significant PDA in premature infants
regimens.quote: premature infants weighing between 500 and 1500 g, who are no more than 32 weeks gestational age

bands.label: Dose 1
bands.quote: An initial dose of 10 mg per kilogram is followed by two doses of 5 mg per kilogram each, after 24 and 48 hours. All doses should be based on birth weight.

bands.label: Doses 2 and 3, at 24 and 48 hours after dose 1
bands.quote: An initial dose of 10 mg per kilogram is followed by two doses of 5 mg per kilogram each, after 24 and 48 hours. All doses should be based on birth weight.

notes.text: Withhold further doses if anuria or marked oliguria (below 0.6 mL/kg/hr) at the time of dose 2 or 3.
notes.quote: If anuria or marked oliguria (urinary output <0.6 mL/kg/hr) is evident at the scheduled time of the second or third dose of Ibuprofen Lysine

notes.text: Do not give in the same IV line as TPN; interrupt TPN for 15 minutes before and after.
notes.quote: If necessary, TPN should be interrupted for a 15-minute period prior to and after drug administration.

regimens.indication: Closure of hemodynamically significant PDA in premature infants
regimens.quote: premature infants weighing between 500 and 1,750 g

bands.label: Age at 1st dose less than 48 hours: dose 1
bands.quote: Less than 48 hours | 1st 0.2 | 2nd 0.1 | 3rd 0.1

bands.label: Age at 1st dose less than 48 hours: doses 2 and 3
bands.quote: Less than 48 hours | 1st 0.2 | 2nd 0.1 | 3rd 0.1

bands.label: Age at 1st dose 2 to 7 days: doses 1 to 3
Age at 1st dose over 7 days: dose 1
Age at 1st dose over 7 days: doses 2 and 3

notes.text: Withhold further doses if anuria or marked oliguria (below 0.6 mL/kg/hr).
notes.quote: If anuria or marked oliguria (urinary output <0.6 mL/kg/hr) is evident at the scheduled time of the second or third dose of Indomethacin for Injection, do not give additional doses

notes.text: Reconstitute with preservative-free diluent; benzyl alcohol is toxic in neonates.
notes.quote: Benzyl alcohol as a preservative has been associated with toxicity in neonates. Therefore, do not use diluents that contain preservatives.

regimens.indication: Maintain ductus arteriosus patency in duct-dependent congenital heart disease
regimens.route: IV continuous infusion (or umbilical artery catheter at ductal opening)

bands.label: Starting infusion
bands.quote: Begin infusion with 0.05 to 0.1 micrograms alprostadil per kilogram of body weight per minute.

bands.label: After response, reduce to the lowest effective rate
bands.quote: This may be accomplished by reducing the dosage from 0.1 to 0.05 to 0.025 to 0.01 micrograms per kilogram of body weight per minute.

bands.label: If response to 0.05 is inadequate, may increase
bands.quote: If response to 0.05 micrograms per kilogram of body weight per minute is inadequate, dosage can be increased up to 0.4 micrograms per kilogram of body weight per minute

notes.text: Boxed warning: apnea in about 10 to 12% of neonates, most often under 2 kg birth weight, usually in the first hour; ventilatory support must be immediately available.
notes.quote: Apnea is experienced by about 10 to 12% of neonates with congenital heart defects treated with PROSTIN VR PEDIATRIC Sterile Solution. Apnea is most often seen in neonates weighing less than 2 kg at birth and usually appears during the first hour of drug infusion.

notes.text: Prepare fresh infusion every 24 hours.
notes.quote: Prepare fresh infusion solutions every 24 hours.

regimens.indication: Hemodynamic support (pediatric dosing reported in publications)

bands.label: Starting dose (publications)
bands.quote: In publications, the most common starting doses were 1-5 micrograms/kilograms/minute.

bands.label: Titration increments (publications)
bands.quote: Dosing increments that were reported ranged from 2.5 to 5.0 micrograms/kilogram/minute.

bands.label: Usual maximum (publications)
bands.quote: Usual maximum doses were 15-20 micrograms/kilogram/minute, with occasional use as great as 50 micrograms/kilogram/minute.

notes.text: Label states pediatric safety and effectiveness not established; doses above are from publications.
notes.quote: Pediatric Use Safety and effectiveness in children have not been established.

notes.text: Neonatal clearance is highly variable; use low doses and slow titration. Newborns may be more sensitive to vasoconstriction.
notes.quote: Because of the variability of clearance, especially in the neonate and newborn, low doses of dopamine and slow deliberate titration should be employed

notes.text: Low neonatal doses require considerable dilution of this premixed product.
notes.quote: Particularly in neonates, such low doses require considerable dilution of this product

notes.text: No neonatal dose in label. In premature neonates dobutamine is less effective than dopamine at raising blood pressure without undue tachycardia.
notes.quote: In premature neonates, however, dobutamine is less effective than dopamine in raising systemic blood pressure without causing undue tachycardia

bands.label: Total IV loading dose, premature
bands.freq: half initially, then one quarter every 6 to 8 hours twice
bands.quote: Administer half the total loading dose initially, then ¼ the loading dose every 6-8 hours twice Premature 15-25

bands.label: Total IV loading dose, full-term
bands.freq: half initially, then one quarter every 6 to 8 hours twice
bands.quote: Administer half the total loading dose initially, then ¼ the loading dose every 6-8 hours twice Premature 15-25 Full-Term 20-30

bands.label: Starting IV maintenance, premature
bands.quote: Dose Regimen, mcg/kg/dose (given TWICE daily) Premature 1.9-3.1

bands.label: Starting IV maintenance, full-term
bands.quote: Dose Regimen, mcg/kg/dose (given TWICE daily) Premature 1.9-3.1 Full-Term 3-4.5

bands.label: Oral loading dose, premature
bands.quote: Premature | 20 to 30

bands.label: Oral loading dose, full-term
bands.quote: Full-Term | 25 to 35

bands.label: Oral maintenance, premature
bands.quote: Premature | 4.7 to 7.8 | 2.3 to 3.9 Twice Daily

bands.label: Oral maintenance, full-term
bands.quote: Full-Term | 7.5 to 11.3 | 3.8 to 5.6 Twice Daily

notes.text: Toxic levels are only slightly higher than therapeutic levels; monitor for toxicity.
notes.quote: toxic levels of digoxin are only slightly higher than therapeutic levels

notes.text: Pediatric IM: no more than 200 mcg of LANOXIN Injection Pediatric per site; IV preferred, avoid bolus.
notes.quote: For pediatric patients, no more than 200 mcg of LANOXIN Injection Pediatric should be injected into a single site. Administer the dose over a period of 5 minutes or longer and avoid bolus administration

regimens.route: IV rapid bolus with saline flush

bands.label: Initial dose, body weight below 50 kg
bands.freq: once; repeat after 1-2 minutes if no conversion
bands.quote: Pediatric Patients with a Body Weight < 50 kg: Initial dose: Give 0.05 to 0.1 mg/kg as a rapid IV bolus

bands.label: Repeat doses: increase by 0.05 to 0.1 mg/kg each bolus
bands.quote: Pediatric Patients with a Body Weight < 50 kg: Initial dose: Give 0.05 to 0.1 mg/kg as a rapid IV bolus given either centrally or peripherally. A saline flush should follow. Repeat administration: If conversion of PSVT does not occur within 1-2 minutes, additional bolus injections of adenosine can be administered at incrementally higher doses, increasing the amount given by 0.05 to 0.1 mg/kg. Follow each bolus with a saline flush. This process should continue until sinus rhythm is established or a maximum single dose of 0.3 mg/kg is used.

notes.text: Label: pediatric doses in neonates were equivalent to adult doses on a weight basis; no controlled pediatric studies.
notes.quote: The dosages used in neonates, infants, children and adolescents were equivalent to those administered to adults on a weight basis.

bands.label: Usual initial dose
bands.freq: may be repeated per adult postoperative guidelines
bands.quote: Usage in Neonates: Opioid-Induced Depression: The usual initial dose is 0.01 mg/kg body weight administered I.V., I.M., or S.C.

notes.text: Use cautiously in newborns of opioid-dependent mothers; abrupt reversal may precipitate withdrawal, including convulsions.
notes.quote: Naloxone hydrochloride injection should be administered cautiously to persons, including newborns of mothers, who are known or suspected to be physically dependent on opioids.

notes.text: No benefit as an additional resuscitation method in intrauterine asphyxia not related to opioids.
notes.quote: Naloxone has no apparent benefit as an additional method of resuscitation in the newly born infant with intrauterine asphyxia, which is not related to opioid use.

regimens.indication: Tracheal intubation and neuromuscular blockade during anesthesia

bands.label: Initial intubation dose, pediatric
bands.quote: The recommended initial intubation dose of Rocuronium Bromide Injection is 0.6 mg/kg; however, a lower dose of 0.45 mg/kg may be used depending on anesthetic technique and the age of the patient.

bands.label: Maintenance bolus at reappearance of T3, all pediatric age groups
bands.quote: ce dosing of Rocuronium Bromide Injection can be administered as bolus doses of 0.15 mg/kg at reappearance of T 3 in all pediatric age groups.

bands.label: Maintenance infusion at reappearance of T2 (lowest requirement in neonates)
bands.quote: Maintenance dosing can also be administered at the reappearance of T 2 at a rate of 7 mcg/kg/min to 10 mcg/kg/min, with the lowest dose requirement for neonates (birth to less than 28 days)

notes.text: Not recommended for rapid sequence intubation in pediatric patients.
notes.quote: Not recommended for rapid sequence intubation in pediatric patients.

notes.text: Time to maximum block after an intubating dose is longest in neonates (birth to less than 28 days).
notes.quote: longest in neonates (birth to less than 28 days).

notes.text: No dosing recommendation under 7 weeks of age; no pediatric continuous infusion recommendation.
notes.quote: Information presently available does not permit recommendation on usage in pediatric patients less than 7 weeks of age

notes.text: Bacteriostatic water (benzyl alcohol) reconstitution is not for use in newborns.
notes.quote: bacteriostatic water for injection ( NOT FOR USE IN NEWBORNS )

regimens.indication: Anticoagulation (pediatric guideline based on clinical experience)

bands.label: Initial bolus
bands.quote: Initial Dose 75 to 100 units/kg (Intravenous bolus over 10 minutes)

bands.label: Maintenance infusion, infants
bands.quote: Infants: 25 to 30 units/kg/hour; Infants < 2 months have the highest requirements (average 28 units/kg/hour)

notes.text: Use preservative-free heparin in neonates and infants (benzyl alcohol toxicity).
notes.quote: Do not use benzyl alcohol-preserved drugs in neonates and infants. Use preservative-free Heparin Sodium Injection in neonates and infants

notes.text: Deaths in neonates from confusing heparin vials with catheter lock flush vials; confirm strength.
notes.quote: Pediatric patients, including neonates, have died as a result of medication errors in which Heparin Sodium Injection vials have been confused with "catheter lock flush" vials

notes.text: Adjust to APTT 60 to 85 seconds (anti-Xa 0.35 to 0.70).
notes.quote: Adjust heparin to maintain APTT of 60 to 85 seconds, assuming this reflects an anti-Factor Xa level of 0.35 to 0.70

regimens.indication: Prophylaxis of hemorrhagic disease of the newborn

bands.label: Single dose within 1 hour of birth
bands.quote: A single intramuscular dose of phytonadione injectable emulsion, USP 0.5 to 1 mg within one hour of birth is recommended.

regimens.indication: Treatment of hemorrhagic disease of the newborn

bands.label: Treatment dose
bands.quote: Phytonadione injectable emulsion, USP 1 mg should be given either subcutaneously or intramuscularly. Higher doses may be necessary if the mother has been receiving oral anticoagulants.

notes.text: Do not exceed the recommended dose: hemolysis, jaundice and hyperbilirubinemia in neonates, especially premature.
notes.quote: Hemolysis, jaundice, and hyperbilirubinemia in neonates, particularly those that are premature, may be related to the dose of phytonadione injectable emulsion. Therefore, the recommended dose should not be exceeded

notes.text: Boxed warning: severe reactions including fatalities with IV and IM use.
notes.quote: Severe reactions, including fatalities, have occurred during and immediately after INTRAVENOUS injection of phytonadione

notes.text: Use only preservative-free diluents (benzyl alcohol toxicity in newborns).
notes.quote: Benzyl alcohol as a preservative has been associated with toxicity in newborns. Therefore, all of the above diluents should be preservative-free

bands.label: Bolus, neonate (1 month or younger)
bands.freq: initial; subsequent doses if needed every 6 hours
bands.infuse: dilute to 10-50 mg/mL; not faster than 100 mg/minute
bands.quote: Neonate (≤ 1 month) 100 - 200 mg/kg 100 - 200 mg/kg every 6 hours Initiate at 17-33 mg/kg/hour

bands.label: Continuous infusion start, neonate (1 month or younger)
bands.infuse: dilute to 5.8-10 mg/mL; adjust to serum calcium
bands.quote: Neonate (≤ 1 month) 100 - 200 mg/kg 100 - 200 mg/kg every 6 hours Initiate at 17-33 mg/kg/hour

notes.text: Bolus rate must not exceed 100 mg/minute in pediatric patients including neonates.
notes.quote: DO NOT exceed an infusion rate of 200 mg/minute in adults or 100 mg/minute in pediatric patients, including neonates.

notes.text: Contraindicated with IV ceftriaxone in neonates 28 days or younger.
notes.quote: Concomitant use of ceftriaxone and intravenous calcium-containing products is contraindicated in neonates (28 days of age or younger)

notes.text: Measure serum calcium every 4 to 6 hours with intermittent and every 1 to 4 hours with continuous infusion.
notes.quote: Measure serum calcium every 4 to 6 hours during intermittent infusions with Calcium Gluconate Injection and measure serum calcium every 1 to 4 hours during continuous infusion.

notes.text: Each mL contains 100 mg calcium gluconate = 9.3 mg (0.465 mEq) elemental calcium.
notes.quote: Calcium Gluconate Injection contains 100 mg of calcium gluconate per mL which contains 9.3 mg (i.e., 0.465 mEq) of elemental calcium.

bands.label: Pediatric patients under 2 years including neonates
bands.infuse: over 4 to 8 hours; avoid rapid or bolus
bands.quote: Recommended Dosage in Pediatric Patients Less Than 2 Years of Age, including Neonates Administer 1 mEq/kg to 2 mEq/kg of sodium bicarbonate injection over a four- to eight-hour period. Avoid rapid or bolus administration

notes.text: Limit rate to no more than 8 mEq/kg/day in neonates and children under 2 years (hypernatremia, intracranial hemorrhage).
notes.quote: Rapid injection of sodium bicarbonate injection solutions into neonates and children under two years of age may produce hypernatremia, a decrease in cerebrospinal fluid pressure and possible intracranial hemorrhage. The rate of administration in such patients should therefore be limited to no more than 8 mEq/kg/day.
